transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining. As you know, we're finalizing the exclusive license agreement with Northlake University covering their medical-device platform patent applications. The current draft grants worldwide exclusivity at a 3% running royalty, and we're scheduled to sign next Monday. Before we can move to execution, the draft requires us to complete patent and regulatory diligence, and the business team is eager to get access to the technology immediately after signing. I've asked each of you — IP, licensing finance, patent prosecution, and export controls — to review the draft and flag any issues that should change our approval package. Let's go around the table. What are you seeing?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a finance issue before we go further. This morning I completed a finance-validated benchmark of three comparable medical-device licenses, and it shows a 225-basis-point running royalty as the approved market ceiling for this technology class. That benchmark was delivered to me this morning and is not in the deal summary. The current draft sets a 3% running royalty, which is 75 basis points above our validated market ceiling. I recommend we renegotiate the royalty rate down to 2.25% or below before signing.

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical patent prosecution issue. My review of the inventor assignment file found that one named inventor never assigned rights in the pending continuation application. The missing assignment must be obtained and recorded before the company can rely on that application. I have not yet circulated my title memorandum on this, so you're all hearing it now for the first time. This directly affects the diligence requirement in the draft — we cannot certify clean title to that continuation application until the missing assignment is secured, and it needs to be addressed as a condition to signing or at minimum as a closing condition.

transcript.text: I need to flag an export controls issue. I completed the export-classification review today and confirmed that the platform is classified as ECCN 3A001 technology. This is critical because ECCN 3A001 is a controlled technology, and the license agreement must include provisions prohibiting transfers to military end users and requiring an annual end-use screening certification. Neither of these export-control terms is in the current draft, and this classification has not yet been added to the transaction checklist. We need these provisions inserted before signing to ensure we're not exposing the company to export-control violations when the business team begins accessing and working with the technology after execution.

transcript.text: I need to flag an IP issue. My review of Northlake's archived grant register found a prior written grant to the University Research Consortium covering academic research and teaching uses. That grant permits the consortium to continue those uses, which means our exclusive license needs a carveout preserving the consortium's existing rights — otherwise we'll have a conflict between our exclusivity and Northlake's prior commitment. I have not yet added this carveout to the license draft, and it needs to be addressed before signing.

I'll add that language to the draft as soon as we've finished discussing all the issues today.
